info.title: retooled-patch
info.description: The retooled-patch command, which builds, checks, applies and reverts KSP Retooled patch files.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: Builds, checks, applies and reverts KSP Retooled patch files (.rtpatch).

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

commands.name: build
commands.description: Builds one patch file that turns each --source install into the --target build. The command also writes a report next to the patch file, named <file>.report.txt.

options.name: --source
options.description: A stock install that the patch should accept. Repeat --source once for each install. If one install is split across several directories, such as a game depot and its DLC depots, list them all, separated by ';' on Windows or ':' elsewhere. A file in a later directory replaces the file at the same path in an earlier one. If you leave out the name, the command reads it from the install's buildID file (for example, steam-03190). If there is no buildID file, it uses the directory name.

options.name: --target
options.description: The KSP Retooled build that the patch should produce.

options.name: --out
options.description: The patch file to write. If the name doesn't end in .rtpatch, the command adds it.

options.name: --platform
options.description: The platform that the patch is for. If you leave it out, the command looks at the game executable in --target to decide.

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Paths to leave out of every source and the target. A built-in list already leaves out saves, logs, settings.cfg and similar files; these patterns add to that list. Patterns are paths relative to the top of the install. In a pattern, '*' matches any characters, including '/', so it can match across directories. To give more than one pattern, repeat the option or separate the patterns with commas. [default: System.String[]]

options.name: --exclude-target
options.description: Paths to leave out of the target only. These use the same patterns as --exclude. [default: System.String[]]

options.name: --copy
options.description: Files or directories that the patch doesn't contain. Each one must be an exact path, not a pattern. When someone applies the patch with --out, the command copies these paths unchanged from their install. To give more than one path, repeat the option or separate the paths with commas. [default: System.String[]]

options.name: --jobs
options.description: How many worker threads to use. By default there is one per CPU core, or fewer if the machine doesn't have enough memory for that many. [default: 4]

options.name: --level
options.description: The zstd compression level. [default: 19]

options.name: --window
options.description: The zstd window size, as a power of 2. For example, 27 is 128 MB. It must be between 10 and 31, which is 2 GB. [default: 27]

commands.name: info
commands.description: Shows what a patch file contains: the platform, the source installs that it accepts, the files that it copies unchanged, its compressed sections, and its DLC components.

options.name: --patch
options.description: The patch file to describe.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Reports which source the install matches, and whether the patch can be applied to it. This command doesn't change any files. It exits with 0 if the patch can be applied, and with 1 if it can't.

options.name: --install
options.description: The KSP install to check.

options.name: --patch
options.description: The patch file to check the install against.

commands.name: apply
commands.description: Patches a stock install so that it becomes KSP Retooled. You must pass either --out or --in-place, but not both. In either case, the command only patches a DLC if that DLC is installed.

options.name: --install
options.description: The stock KSP install to patch.

options.name: --patch
options.description: The patch file to apply.

options.name: --out
options.description: Writes a patched copy of the install to <new-dir>, and leaves the original install unchanged. [Group: 'mode', required]

options.name: --in-place
options.description: Patches the install directly. Before the command replaces a stock file, it saves that file in <ksp-dir>/.retooled, so that revert can restore it later. [Group: 'mode', required] [default: False]

commands.name: revert
commands.description: Undoes an in-place apply, so that the install is stock again. Your saves and settings aren't changed.

options.name: --install
options.description: The install that was patched with apply --in-place.
